title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
summary: Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer value, locate the node with that value and return the subtree rooted at that node.
statement: Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer value, locate the node with that value and return the subtree rooted at that node. If no such node exists, return null.
constraints: The input is a BST with 1–5000 nodes. Node values and val are in [1, 10^7].
Return the complete subtree rooted at the matching node, or None (displayed as []) if absent.

hints: The BST ordering tells you which single branch can contain the target.
Compare at each node: smaller goes left, larger goes right, equal returns that node.
Repeat until finding val or reaching None. Return the node itself, with its children still attached.
Do not return only its value or construct a leaf copy; the output is a subtree.
editorial: At each node, BST ordering rules out the entire right subtree for a smaller target and the entire left subtree for a larger one. Follow the remaining branch until equality or a missing child. Returning the matching node preserves all of its descendants. This takes O(h) time and constant extra space iteratively; a recursive version needs O(h) call-stack space.
